Holiday payroll calendar for December 2026 and January 2027
Between late November 2026 and early February 2027, the Federal Reserve observes Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26, Christmas on Friday, December 25, New Year’s Day on Friday, January 1 and Martin Luther King Jr. Day on Monday, January 18. Because ACH payments are not currently settled on weekends and federal holidays, a direct deposit payday on any of those dates needs a different settlement date. Federal tax deposits and filings run on a separate calendar.
What does the payroll calendar look like from Thanksgiving to early February?
As of October 2026, the dates below run from Wednesday, November 25, 2026, to Wednesday, February 10, 2027. Three separate calendars sit behind them. The Federal Reserve holiday list decides when direct deposit settles. IRS rules decide when federal payroll tax deposits and filings are due. A payroll provider’s and a bank’s cutoffs and closure days are set by contract, so each one needs to be confirmed in writing.

Which bank holidays pause direct deposit, and how does that change payday timing?
Direct deposit pauses on four Federal Reserve holidays in this window, Thursday, November 26, Friday, December 25, Friday, January 1 and Monday, January 18, because ACH settlement runs only when the Federal Reserve’s National Settlement Service is open. Nacha says ACH credits can settle the same day, the next banking day or in two banking days. The effective entry date is the banking day the originator of the payment file intends a batch of entries to settle. A pay date on a Federal Reserve holiday cannot be a settlement date, so the effective entry date has to be a banking day before or after it.


As of October 2026, if the provider and its bank offer it, Same Day ACH settles at 1:00 p.m., 5:00 p.m. and 6:00 p.m. Eastern Time and is limited to $1 million per payment until a rule raising the limit to $10 million takes effect September 17, 2027. Offering Same Day ACH is optional for the sending bank, so it is the provider’s and its bank’s call. Since September 18, 2026, a receiving bank must make non-same-day credits available by 9:00 a.m. local time on the settlement date. That rule sets when funds must be available, not when a deposit posts.


The Federal Reserve’s deadlines bind the sending bank, and the employer’s payroll cutoff is set by the provider. Before a holiday payroll, get the answers to these questions in writing.


* Ask for the payroll cutoff and its time zone.
* Ask how many banking days before the pay date payroll must be approved.
* Ask whether Same Day ACH is offered and for which payrolls.
* Ask which holiday calendar the provider and its bank follow.
* Ask how an effective entry date that falls on a weekend or holiday is handled.
* Ask on what date the funding debit is taken, because many payroll files are funded using an ACH debit that runs on its own clock.


Hypothetical example. An employer’s regular payday is Friday, December 25, 2026, and direct deposit cannot settle that day. Assume the provider needs payroll approved N banking days before the settlement date. N stands for the number in the provider’s written terms and is not any provider’s rule.


* Pay the prior banking day. Settlement moves to Thursday, December 24, and approval is due N banking days before that, one banking day earlier than an ordinary Friday settlement on December 25 would require.
* Pay the next banking day. Settlement moves to Monday, December 28. Friday, December 25 is not a banking day, so the count back from Monday skips it, and approval falls on the same date an ordinary Friday settlement would require.


Whether a state’s payday rules allow either choice is a separate question, covered below.
How do holidays move federal payroll tax deposit dates?
A federal payroll tax deposit due on a day that is not a business day is timely if it is made by the close of the next business day. Publication 15 defines a business day as any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, and for deposits a legal holiday means a District of Columbia legal holiday, so a statewide holiday does not delay a federal tax deposit. Publication 15’s 2026 list of legal holidays includes Thanksgiving Day and Christmas Day and leaves out December 24 and December 31. As of October 2026, the IRS’s 2027 legal holiday list appears only in draft publications, which list January 1, January 18 and February 15, 2027 as legal holidays, the same dates the Federal Reserve observes.


Semiweekly depositors deposit payments made Wednesday to Friday by the following Wednesday and payments made Saturday to Tuesday by the following Friday. The deposit is due at least three business days after the semiweekly period closes, and a depositor gets an additional day for each legal holiday among the three weekdays after the period ends.


Pay dates in two different quarters get separate deposits for the separate liabilities. Wages paid Thursday, December 31, 2026, are fourth-quarter wages, and wages paid Monday, January 4, 2027, are first-quarter wages. Because the clock follows the dates wages are paid, moving a payday across a holiday or December 31 can move the deposit date and can move the quarter.


The $100,000 rule applies to both schedules. Once a depositor accumulates $100,000 or more in taxes on any day, the deposit is due by the next business day. That makes a $100,000 liability reached on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, due Friday, November 27, and one reached on Thursday, December 24, due Monday, December 28.


For the Christmas hypothetical above, an employer that pays Thursday, December 24, owes a semiweekly deposit on Wednesday, December 30, 2026. Paying Monday, December 28, puts the semiweekly deposit on Friday, January 1, a holiday, so it is due Monday, January 4, 2027. A monthly depositor’s federal tax deposit for December wages is due Friday, January 15, 2027, either way.


As of October 2026, EFTPS.gov says payments must be scheduled by 8 p.m. ET the day before the due date, and that payments through third parties may have earlier cutoff times. Publication 15 adds that a same-day EFTPS payment of $1 million or less needs to be submitted before 3:00 p.m. Eastern time on a business day, and it describes a same-day wire arranged ahead with the employer’s bank, with availability, deadlines and costs to check first. The same publication says an employer generally remains responsible if a third party hired to make deposits fails to perform a required action.
Which federal filings land in January and early February 2027?
January 31, 2027, is a Sunday, so the January 31 deadlines move to Monday, February 1, 2027. The fourth-quarter Form 941 is due the last day of the month after the quarter ends, and a return due on a weekend or legal holiday may be filed the next business day. Form 1099-NEC is due January 31, or the next business day on a weekend or holiday. Forms W-2 and W-3 for 2026 are due February 1, 2027, with the Social Security Administration, and employee copies of Form W-2 are due the same day.


Form 941 has a later filing date, the 10th day of the second month after the quarter ends, when the employer made timely deposits in full payment of the taxes for the quarter. For the fourth quarter of 2026, that date is Wednesday, February 10, 2027. Form 940 is due January 31, or February 10 if all federal unemployment (FUTA) tax was deposited when due, so the 2026 Form 940 is due Monday, February 1, 2027, or Wednesday, February 10, on the same condition.


If the fourth-quarter FUTA liability plus any amount not yet deposited is over $500, the entire amount is deposited by the Form 940 due date, Monday, February 1, 2027. An amount of $500 or less may be deposited or paid with Form 940, also by that date.


A FUTA credit reduction, when one applies, is a fourth-quarter liability and goes with the fourth-quarter deposit. As of October 2026, the 2026 list is not final. The IRS says the Department of Labor announces any credit reduction states after the November 10 deadline each year, and the Department of Labor says the final reduction for a year is not determined until November 10 of that year.


AsureCentral covers payroll tax filing for growing employers.
What do wage laws say about holiday paydays, and which year do the wages count in?
The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), the federal wage and hour law, requires FLSA wages to be paid on the regular payday for the pay period covered. The Department of Labor’s Handy Reference Guide to the FLSA lists holiday pay and premium pay for weekend or holiday work among the payments the FLSA does not require.


Rules for a payday that falls on a weekend or holiday vary by state, so the state labor agency is the place to check. New Jersey’s wage payment poster says that when a payday falls on a non-work day, payment “shall be made on the immediately preceding work day,” unless a collective bargaining agreement provides otherwise. California’s Labor Commissioner goes the other way in its enforcement manual, which lets an employer pay wages due on a Saturday or Sunday, or on a holiday listed in the California Government Code that the employer has scheduled as a holiday, on the next business day. That is an enforcement position, not a statute.


Wages are reported in the year they are paid. The IRS’s example in the General Instructions for Forms W-2 and W-3 is work from December 13 to 26, 2026, paid January 1, 2027, which goes on the 2027 Form W-2.


Hypothetical example. A biweekly employer pays every other Friday starting January 2, 2026, which makes 26 paydays in 2026, from January 2 to December 18. The next regular payday, Friday, January 1, 2027, is a Federal Reserve holiday and covers work from December 13 to 26, 2026. Each employee earns $2,000 gross per payday, an illustrative figure.


* Pay Thursday, December 31, 2026. That is 27 paydays in 2026, and 27 times $2,000 equals $54,000 of 2026 wages. They belong on the 2026 Form W-2, the fourth-quarter 2026 Form 941 and, for a monthly depositor, the December deposit.
* Pay Monday, January 4, 2027. That is 26 paydays in 2026, and 26 times $2,000 equals $52,000 of 2026 wages. The $2,000 paid on January 4 is 2027 wages, which belong on the 2027 Form W-2, the first-quarter 2027 Form 941 and, for a monthly depositor, the January deposit.


The difference in 2026 wages is $54,000 minus $52,000, or $2,000 per employee. The example counts gross wages paid and does not model withholding.
Frequently asked questions
Does direct deposit settle on bank holidays?
According to Nacha, ACH direct deposit is not currently settled on weekends or federal holidays, so Thursday, November 26, Friday, December 25, Friday, January 1 and Monday, January 18 are not settlement days this season.
What happens when a payroll tax deposit is due on a holiday?
A federal deposit due on a District of Columbia legal holiday is on time if it is made by the close of the next business day, according to Publication 15, and a statewide holiday does not move it. Semiweekly depositors also get an extra day for each legal holiday among the three weekdays after the deposit period ends.
When are the fourth-quarter Form 941, Form 940, Form W-2 and Form 1099-NEC due for 2026?
The fourth-quarter 2026 Form 941, the 2026 Form 940, Form W-2 and Form 1099-NEC are all due Monday, February 1, 2027, because January 31 is a Sunday. Form 941 and Form 940 also have a later filing date, Wednesday, February 10, 2027, available only when all tax was deposited on time and in full.
Does paying a day earlier or later at year-end change the tax year of wages?
Paying a day earlier or later at year-end can change the tax year of wages, because wages are reported in the year they are paid. A payday on Thursday, December 31, 2026, counts as 2026 wages, and a payday on Friday, January 1, 2027, counts as 2027 wages.
